temporal_coverage: 4 baseline years per AOI; 2017-2020 for manavgat/mugla/evia_extended, 2018-2021 for bejis
aggregation: nanmean over 4 yearly QA-masked window medians; window ends on the AOI-specific anniversary of predictor_end_date
scientific_suitability: NOT a climate normal. 4 years not 30; reference period differs for bejis; anniversary date and window width differ per AOI (07-27/08-14/07-28/08-02, 56/60/57/58 days); cloud coverage 47.8-77.3 percent; single variable; clear-sky surface temperature confounded with the land cover and vegetation state the AoA already measures.
notes: The closest multi-year artifact in the repository, and still not usable. Six independent defects; defect 6 (LST is not air temperature and is collinear with the predictors) is decisive on its own.

aggregation: nanstd over the 4 yearly window medians
scientific_suitability: Interannual spread of 4 samples. Not a climate variable; an n=4 dispersion estimate.
notes: Used as the denominator of lst_anomaly_mean. Not a climate normal.

data_source: derived from Landsat LST and NDVI
aggregation: ndvi_binned_dry_wet_edge_tvdi over the baseline composites
scientific_suitability: Inherits every defect of baseline_lst_mean and adds full dependence on the AOI-internal NDVI-LST feature space, which current_tvdi_mean and tvdi_difference_mean already contribute to the predictor-space dissimilarity.
notes: Doubly disqualified: not a climate normal, and collinear with existing predictors.

aggregation: yearly QA-masked window medians
scientific_suitability: Vegetation state, not climate. Also already represented in the predictor set via ndvi_mean.
notes: 4 files per AOI. Same anniversary-window and reference-period mismatches.

temporal_coverage: single fire season; the experiment predictor window only
aggregation: mean/std over daily scenes within the predictor window
scientific_suitability: EVENT-PERIOD, not climate. The artifact metadata states verbatim: 'experiment predictor window (single-season mean/std over daily MODIS scenes within the window), NOT a multi-year baseline'.
notes: Rejects itself in its own metadata. Windows differ per AOI and bejis is a different year entirely.

aggregation: median over the 56-60 day predictor window
scientific_suitability: Event-period model predictor. Already inside the weighted dissimilarity.
notes: Using it as climate would double-count it and is the exact mislabelling the task prohibits.

aggregation: dry/wet edge TVDI over the predictor window
scientific_suitability: Event-period model predictor.
notes: Same.

aggregation: model output over the predictor window
scientific_suitability: Event-period model predictor.
notes: Same.

aggregation: fused Landsat + downscaled over the predictor window
scientific_suitability: Event-period model predictor.
notes: Same.

aggregation: (current_median - baseline_mean) / baseline_std
scientific_suitability: Contains a multi-year term but is a standardised anomaly OF THE EVENT SEASON, not a climatology. Its AOI mean measures how unusual that summer was -- a legitimate quantity, and not a climatic distance between AOIs.
notes: Superficially the most tempting candidate; still an event-period predictor already inside the AoA.

aggregation: mean over the 500 m cell
scientific_suitability: A strong climate proxy in Mediterranean terrain, but already the top-weighted predictor in three of four AOIs. Recycling it as climate would make the two components near-duplicates.
notes: Fallback dataset USGS/SRTMGL1_003.

aggregation: dominant class over the 500 m cell
scientific_suitability: Static land cover, not climate. Already a predictor.
notes: Static land cover, not climate. Already a predictor. The earlier proposal to use it as the climate land mask is SUPERSEDED: the accepted mask is TerraClimate's own native valid-land support.

aggregation: source-vs-target classifier AUC
scientific_suitability: A learned separability measure over the same predictors, not an independent climatic axis. The artifact itself disclaims being a geographic distance.
notes: AUC 0.99987 / 0.99979 / 0.98224 for the three available pairs. Evia absent.

aggregation: mean of (tmmx+tmmn)/2 over all months, arithmetic mean over valid TerraClimate land pixels inside the canonical AOI bbox
scientific_suitability: 30-year WMO normal, shared reference period, shared seasonal definition, independent of the Landsat/MODIS predictor products. Satisfies all seven acceptance criteria in doc 04 section 4.
notes: Scale factor 0.1 C; must be read from band metadata at export time, not hard-coded.

aggregation: mean of (tmmx+tmmn)/2 over months 6-9, land-masked AOI mean
scientific_suitability: Near-duplicate of the annual axis beside it. In a Mediterranean climate the warm-season and annual signals are strongly collinear, so including both would weight the temperature and precipitation directions twice each in an equally-weighted metric, downweighting the deficit and VPD axes.
notes: Proposed in the six-variable draft; REMOVED from the accepted four-variable vector (decision C-8).

aggregation: mean over years of the annual sum of pr, arithmetic mean over valid TerraClimate land pixels inside the canonical AOI bbox
scientific_suitability: Moisture supply axis. Entirely absent from the repository at present.
notes: No precipitation product of any kind exists in the repository today.

aggregation: mean over years of the Jun-Sep sum of pr, land-masked AOI mean
scientific_suitability: Near-duplicate of the annual axis beside it. In a Mediterranean climate the warm-season and annual signals are strongly collinear, so including both would weight the temperature and precipitation directions twice each in an equally-weighted metric, downweighting the deficit and VPD axes.
notes: Proposed in the six-variable draft; REMOVED from the accepted four-variable vector (decision C-8).

aggregation: mean over years of the Jun-Sep sum of def, arithmetic mean over valid TerraClimate land pixels inside the canonical AOI bbox
scientific_suitability: The canonical fire-climate covariate: integrates temperature and moisture supply into the quantity governing fuel dryness. Native to TerraClimate; would have to be derived under ERA5-Land.
notes: The single strongest reason to prefer TerraClimate over ERA5-Land.

aggregation: mean of vpd over months 6-9, arithmetic mean over valid TerraClimate land pixels inside the canonical AOI bbox
scientific_suitability: Atmospheric moisture demand axis, distinct from supply.
notes: Scale factor 0.01 kPa; read from band metadata at export time.

aggregation: temperature_2m, total_precipitation_sum, dewpoint_temperature_2m; same season months
scientific_suitability: Independent reanalysis cross-check. At ~11 km the smallest AOI (bejis, ~60x52 km) spans only about 5x5 cells, too coarse to resolve the coastal/inland contrast that drives the Bejis result.
notes: Removed from the primary completion work (decision C-8). Recorded only as a possible later sensitivity, which would need its own preregistration.

aggregation: 19 bioclimatic variables
scientific_suitability: Finest resolution of the candidates, but the reference period is fixed at 1960-1990 and cannot be changed, and there is no moisture-deficit axis.
notes: A 1960-1990 normal is stale for a 2021/2022 fire-climate question.

aggregation: daily precipitation
scientific_suitability: Precipitation only; a single axis cannot constitute a climate vector.
notes: Would need to be combined with a separate temperature product, which TerraClimate already provides in one collection.

aggregation: same four variables over valid TerraClimate land pixels of lon[-10,42] lat[30,47]; supplies ref_mean and population SD (ddof=0)
scientific_suitability: Supplies ref_mean and ref_sd for the standardisation, so the scale does not come from the four AOIs themselves and does not change when a fifth AOI is added.
notes: Not an AOI. Fixed reference window supplying ref_mean and ref_sd so the scale does not come from the four AOIs and does not change when a fifth is added. All four AOIs lie strictly inside it. Same native TerraClimate land support as the AOI summaries -- one mask definition throughout.
